# P10 — Ruth 3:14-18

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** The nameless dawn: six measures home, and sit still
- **BCV:** Ruth 3:14-18
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** HISTORICAL_NARRATIVE
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
The whole passage sits in INFORMAL_CASUAL. Scene 1 shifts to CONSULTATIVE at scene level, as in the night at the threshing floor; the dawn is still private — before one person could recognize another, and under Boaz's word that it must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor (3:14). Scene 2 shifts to INTIMATE at scene level: Ruth and her mother-in-law talk together (3:16–18), as in 3:1–5. The narrator's voice frames the movements plainly.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
The passage tells the morning after the night at the threshing floor, and Ruth's coming to her mother-in-law. Ruth lies at the place of his feet until the morning and rises before one person could recognize another; and he says: let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor. Then he says: hold out the cloak that is on you; she holds it, and he measures six measures of barley and lays it on her, and he goes into the town. She comes to her mother-in-law, who asks: who are you, my daughter? Ruth tells her all that the man did for her, and says: these six measures of barley he gave me, for he said to me, do not go empty to your mother-in-law. And Naomi says: sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls — for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today. What weighs on the passage is Boaz's word that it must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor, the six measures of barley with his words "do not go empty to your mother-in-law", and Naomi's word to sit still until she knows how the matter falls.

### 2.2 Context
This follows the night at the threshing floor (3:6–13). At night Boaz said: lie down until the morning (3:13); here she lies at the place of his feet until the morning. His word "let it not be known" is the word of Naomi's plan, "do not be known to the man" (3:3). Here the story calls Boaz "he" and "the man", Ruth "the woman" and "my daughter", and Naomi "her mother-in-law". Naomi's question, "who are you, my daughter?", uses the words Boaz asked at night, "who are you?" (3:9). Boaz's words as Ruth reports them, "do not go empty (reqam) to your mother-in-law", use the word of Naomi's "YHWH brought me back empty (reqam)" (1:21). The narrator does not tell Boaz saying those words at the threshing floor; they are heard only in Ruth's report. He goes into the town; she comes to her mother-in-law.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
Quick, and then still. The dawn moves in short motions — lying, rising before one person could recognize another, two instructions, the cloak held out, the barley measured out, his going into the town. With her mother-in-law the question and the telling come quickly, and Ruth speaks of the six measures of barley. Then the passage ends slowly — sit still, my daughter. Naomi's last words are about the man: he will not rest unless he has finished the matter today.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage tells the end of the night at the threshing floor and Ruth's coming to her mother-in-law. Boaz says: let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor. The word "empty" (reqam) of Naomi's 1:21 is said again, in Boaz's words as Ruth reports them: do not go empty to your mother-in-law. Naomi asks "who are you, my daughter?", with the words Boaz asked at night, "who are you?" (3:9). And it ends on Naomi's words: sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls, for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today. To speak this passage is to keep the secret Boaz asked for (3:14), the six measures of barley with his words "do not go empty to your mother-in-law", and Naomi's word to sit still.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — The dawn at the floor: the secrecy word and the six measures (3:14–15)

**3A — Beings**

[[B9-Ruth]] — הָאִשָּׁה / "the woman"
- Role: the one who lies at the place of his feet until the morning, rises before one person could recognize another, and holds the cloak
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- Referential form: "the woman" in Boaz's words (3:14); the narrator says "she"
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B13-Boaz]] — implied speaker
- Role: the one who says "let it not be known", measures the six measures, and goes into the town
- Relationship: a redeemer (3:12); at night he said: if the nearer redeemer will redeem you, good; if he does not want to redeem you, I will redeem you (3:12–13)
- Referential form: "he" (3:14–15)
- Presence: PRESENT

**3B — Places**

[[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] — הַגֹּרֶן / the threshing floor
- Role: where Ruth lay until the morning
- Type: the working-floor where grain is winnowed
- Effect on scene: named in Boaz's words — "let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor"

[[PL4-The-City]] — הָעִיר / the town
- Role: where he goes (3:15)
- Type: the town the two women live in (Bethlehem, named here only as "the town")
- Effect on scene: where he goes after he lays the barley on her

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0042-Uncover-Feet-Margelot]] — מַרְגְּלֹתָיו / "the place of his feet"
- What it is: the place of his feet
- Function in scene: where Ruth lay until the morning — the word of Naomi's plan and of the night (3:4, 7, 8), said a fourth time here

[[O13-Your-Garments]] — הַמִּטְפַּחַת / "the cloak"
- What it is: the outer wrap Ruth is wearing — the word here is mitpachat, not the simlah of 3:3
- Function in scene: she holds it, and he measures six measures of barley and lays it on her

[[O16-Six-Barley]] — שֵׁשׁ־שְׂעֹרִים / "six of barley"
- What it is: six measures of barley — the measure-unit is left unsaid by the text
- Function in scene: measured out by Boaz and laid on her

**3D — Times**

[[TM_NIGHT_TO_MORNING-Night-to-Morning]] — עַד־הַבֹּקֶר … בְּטֶרֶם / "until the morning … before"
- What it is: the morning — at night Boaz said "lie down until the morning" (3:13); she lies until the morning
- Function: she rises before one person could recognize another

**3E — What Happens**
[[B9-Ruth]] She lies at the place of his feet until the morning, and rises before one person could recognize another. [[B13-Boaz]] He says: let it not be known that the woman came to the [[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] floor. He says: hold out the cloak that is on you — and she holds it, and he measures six measures of barley and lays it on her. And he goes into the [[PL4-The-City]] town.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Ruth lies at the place of his feet until the morning and rises before one person could recognize another. Boaz says: let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor. He says: hold out the cloak that is on you; she holds it, and he measures six measures of barley and lays it on her, and he goes into the town.

**Significant Absence**
The narrator tells no farewell. The narrator does not tell Boaz saying "do not go empty to your mother-in-law" at the threshing floor; those words are heard only in Ruth's report (3:17). The text says "six of barley" and does not say six of what measure.

### Scene 2 — To her mother-in-law: the question, the report, and "sit still" (3:16–18)

**3A — Beings**

[[B3-Naomi]] — חֲמוֹתָהּ / "her mother-in-law"
- Role: the one who asks "who are you, my daughter?", hears Ruth's report, and tells her to sit still
- Relationship: mother-in-law of [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth; in Boaz's words, as Ruth reports them, "your mother-in-law"
- Referential form: "her mother-in-law" (3:16); "your mother-in-law" in Boaz's words (3:17)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — בִּתִּי / "my daughter"
- Role: the one questioned, the reporter of all the man did, the bearer of the six measures
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi
- Referential form: "my daughter" in Naomi's mouth (3:16, 3:18)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B13-Boaz]] — הָאִישׁ / "the man"
- Role: the one reported on — what he did, what he gave, and what he said
- Relationship: a redeemer (3:12); in Naomi's words, the man who will not rest unless he has finished the matter today
- Referential form: "the man" (3:16, 3:18); "he" in Ruth's words (3:17)
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

- None: the text names no place in this scene.

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[O16-Six-Barley]] — שֵׁשׁ־הַשְּׂעֹרִים הָאֵלֶּה / "these six of barley"
- What it is: the same six measures, now shown
- Function in scene: Ruth says: these six measures of barley he gave me

[[CB_0044-Riqam-Empty]] — רֵיקָם / "empty"
- What it is: the empty-word — empty-handed, emptied out
- Function in scene: the word Boaz's reported speech forbids — do not go empty to your mother-in-law
- Cross-ref: the same word as Naomi's at 1:21, "YHWH brought me back empty"

[[CB_0024-Full-and-Empty]] — רֵיקָם / "empty" (of Naomi's pair "full … empty", 1:21)
- What it is: the pair of words in Naomi's 1:21, "I went out full, and YHWH brought me back empty"
- Function in scene: of the pair, only "empty" is said here, in Boaz's words as Ruth reports them

[[CB_0043-Mother-in-Law-Chamot]] — חֲמוֹתֵךְ / "your mother-in-law"
- What it is: the mother-in-law word — the kinship role itself
- Function in scene: in Boaz's words, as Ruth reports them: do not go empty to your mother-in-law

[[O19-Word]] — דָּבָר / "the matter"
- What it is: the matter (davar); Naomi does not say what the matter is
- Function in scene: what Ruth must wait to see fall, and what the man will not rest until he has finished — twice named in Naomi's closing word

**3D — Times**

[[TM_TODAY-Today]] — הַיּוֹם / "today"
- What it is: the day now beginning
- Function: in Naomi's words, the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today — "today" goes with finishing the matter

**3E — What Happens**
[[B9-Ruth]] She comes to [[B3-Naomi]] her mother-in-law. Naomi says: who are you, my daughter? And Ruth tells her all that [[B13-Boaz]] the man did for her. She says: these six measures of barley he gave me, for he said to me, do not go empty to your mother-in-law. And Naomi says: sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls — for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Ruth comes to her mother-in-law, who asks: who are you, my daughter? Ruth tells her all that the man did for her, and says: these six measures of barley he gave me, for he said to me, do not go empty to your mother-in-law. Naomi tells her to sit still until she knows how the matter falls, for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today.

**Significant Absence**
To Naomi's question, Ruth tells her all that the man did for her. The narrator does not tell Boaz saying "do not go empty" at the threshing floor; it is heard only in Ruth's report.
